title: Internal Tables Are Not Evidence Until You Can Read Them
description: On 12 April 2026 file and scan-session records become inspectable through read-only routes. The API is not a loose write channel.
body:
A platform that stores records it cannot show has a private diary, not an evidence base. If the only way to know what was scanned is to read the database by hand, the working method is still folklore. People and agents need a door that is allowed, limited, and honest about what it will not do.

On 12 April 2026 I wire GET /files to the files table with the primary classification joined, and GET /scan/sessions plus GET /scan/{id} to the scan-session table. Those list endpoints had been empty or missing. They now return what the tables actually hold. The same morning the capture-thought handler is aligned so a missing thread is passed as none instead of breaking the call, and the tool schemas expose the project and track fields the thought table already had.

A scan session without a duration, a start, and an end is a rumor of work. Wiring the session table means a later reader can ask how long a pass took and which identifier it used. Wiring files means the same reader can see the path and the primary process code together. That is a small sentence in an API. It is a large change in whether the index can be examined without sitting on the database.

The wrong default

The usual move is to add a write API because reads feel unimpressive. That is how an index becomes a second, poorly governed store. These routes are list and detail. They are not a scan-start. They are not a place to pour new files in. Admission of enterprise content is a different job, later the same day.

A glass door on an archive is still a door. You can see the shelves. You cannot rearrange them by looking. Access rules have to be visible: what enters, what is recorded about it, and what remains outside the claim. A file result that carries its primary APQC classification is already more honest than a bare path.

What this does not claim

There is no permission model on these list routes yet. There is no write path. A bad session id returns an error instead of a guess. Duration is computed from the session’s own start and end, not invented. Pagination is limit and offset on files, filtered by type if you ask. That is enough to make the intake inspectable. It is not enough to call the platform a governed vault.

The capture-thought fix is small and necessary. A memory service that throws when the thread is absent is a service people will stop using. Aligning the handler with the thought service is part of making the March surface callable from the April routes, not a new philosophy of memory.

The next test

The next work is whether a person can follow a scan session to the files it produced and see the classification that was attached, without the route pretending to be a memory of things it did not store. The same day’s connector and model work will ask a larger question. This piece is only the glass door.

Historical basis: VALESKA commits e2a6bea, b6ab8d7, and b1babc4, April 12, 2026.

data.coverAlt: A stone library opening through a luminous doorway into rows of inspectable records: internal tables exposed as read-only evidence, not a write channel.
